You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: pass: The mug is visibly to the right of the headphones. fail: The mug is visibly not to the right of the headphones. unknown: Their relative positions cannot be determined from the image.
node.binding: Inspect the edited image and compare the mug’s position with the headphones; this directly tests the requested outcome.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the mug is visibly to the right of the headphones.

fulfillment: The node’s evidence supports that a mug is right of the headphones in the edited image, but that alone does not establish the requested edit: the source already has the mug left of the headphones, and the edited image appears to contain multiple mugs, including one still left of the headphones and another right of them. The trace’s claim that the mug’s position changed is therefore ambiguous about object identity and does not establish that the original target mug was moved; its 0.99 confidence and “complete” status are not justified by the stated evidence. Tighten the binding to track the source mug across images and require the decision to distinguish moving that mug from duplicating or adding a mug. Use the rubric’s partial outcome when there is evidence of progress but completion is not established, and unknown if identity or change cannot be resolved. Keep the existing dependencies only if they provide this source-to-edited identity and progress evidence; otherwise repair their evidence routing. This is a semantic evidence/binding issue, not a transport or schema failure.
s2: The node asks whether any relative-position change occurred, which can pass on an added duplicate and overstate progress. Bind the comparison to the source mug’s visual identity and assess whether that mug itself moved relative to the headphones; distinguish movement from an added mug while allowing genuine partial progress without requiring full completion. The images show the original blue mug left of the headphones, while the edit appears to contain a blue remnant/blur on the left and two smaller mugs, one on each side; this raises identity and edit-extent ambiguity rather than proving the original mug was moved. Require evidence for source-to-edit correspondence and calibrated confidence; use unknown when correspondence or change is unresolved, and do not infer completion from a mug merely appearing on the right. Preserve the rubric’s partial outcome when supported progress exists but fulfillment is incomplete. This is a semantic binding/evidence issue, not a transport or schema failure.
